deities: Goddess Ambika (form of Durga, worshipped as Shakti)

history.dynasty: Mewar (Guhila); present complex rebuilt by Rana Raimal in the late 15th century
history.period: Present complex 15th century (the Ambika shrine itself is undated in consulted sources)
history.summary: FLAG: this is NOT the same temple as seq 2121's Ambika Mata Temple at Jagat (the 10th-century 'Khajuraho of Mewar', ~50 km southeast of Udaipur). This row covers the Ambamata shrine inside the Eklingji temple complex at Kailashpuri village - one of the many small shrines among the 108 temples of the complex; templenet lists 'small temples dedicated to Ambamata, Kalka Mata and Ganesh' alongside the main four-faced Shiva shrine. The Eklingji complex itself: originally associated with the 8th-century Bappa Rawal (per the Ekalinga Mahatmya), destroyed in Delhi Sultanate invasions, rebuilt by Hamir Singh (14th c.) and Rana Kumbha (15th c.), with the present form patronized by Rana Raimal with the ransom from Ghiyath Shah of Malwa. It is the kuladevata (ruling deity) of Mewar, with the Maharanas ruling as Eklingji's Dewan. CSV town 'Eklingji' corrected to Kailashpuri (the village at Girwa tehsil where the complex stands). Coordinates are the geocoded Eklingji complex (24.74677, 73.72284) and are approximate for the sub-shrine (verify). Media image depicts the Eklingji complex, not the Ambika shrine itself - no published image of the specific shrine was found.

name: Ambika Mata Temple, Eklingji
town_description: Kailashpuri (popularly called Eklingji after its great temple) is a temple town in Udaipur district, Rajasthan, about 22 km north of Udaipur in a valley near the former Mewar capital of Nagda. It is dominated by the fortified Eklingji temple complex with its 108 shrines and is one of Mewar's principal pilgrimage centres.

travel.airport: Maharana Pratap Airport (Udaipur), about 25 km away (verify).
travel.railway: Udaipur City railway station, about 22 km away (verify).
travel.road: Kailashpuri, about 22 km north of Udaipur near Nagda; reached by taxi or auto-rickshaw on the Udaipur-Nathdwara road.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri for the complex's main festival.
visitor_information.opening_hours: One source lists the complex at 4:30-7:00 AM, 10:30 AM-1:30 PM and 5:00-7:30 PM - verify; the Ambika sub-shrine's own hours are not published.
